claims.claim: A 2004 Journal of Economic Perspectives paper finds that U.S. presidential betting markets from 1868 to 1940 forecast elections well before scientific polling, were fairly efficient despite limited information and manipulation attempts, and largely disappeared because of scientific polls and other gambling.
claims.episode_span: Between 1868 and 1940, large and often well-organized markets took bets on U.S. presidential elections.
claims.supporting_quote: This paper analyzes the large and often well-organized markets for betting on U.S. presidential elections that operated between 1868 and 1940.
